tools.name: get_dmarc_record
tools.description:
DMARC record, policy, and whether it actually protects.

Returns the DMARC TXT record at _dmarc.<domain>, its policy (none / quarantine / reject), the percentage it applies to, and whether that policy protects against spoofing. Also flags the case of MULTIPLE DMARC records, which RFC 7489 requires r

tools.name: get_mx_records
tools.description:
Mail exchanger records for a domain.

Returns the MX hosts in priority order and whether any exist. A domain with no MX records cannot receive mail, so sending to it will bounce. Use when you only need deliverability and not spoofing posture; use check_email_domain for the full picture.

tools.description:

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "email-check-b6ab5250" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_email_domain · Private data: check_email_domain, get_dmarc_record, get_mx_records, get_spf_record · Public sink: check_email_domain.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_email_domain · Private data: check_email_domain, get_dmarc_record, get_mx_records, get_spf_record · Public sink: check_email_domain

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
